headline: On a real composed tab group the css-prop fold merges the whole chain into one className and beats `vanilla` on SSR CPU, while the styled perf runtime keeps a residual `Yak` on its `styled(Component)` seams and sits mid-pack.

microbench.why: The css-prop fold concatenates every composition level into one className on the plain element, so `next-yak-css-9.7` renders at 0.842 ms/1k, next to `vanilla` (0.813). The styled perf runtime cannot flatten the `styled(Tabs)` and `styled(TabInternal)` seams to a single element, so a residual `Yak` renders per group and it sits at 1.45 ms/1k, 1.7× the css-prop path. The hashers trail, `styled-components` 2.92 ms/1k, `emotion` 5.78 re-serializing per element.

autocannon.why: Under load the single-class css-prop fold serves 669 req/s, within 7% of `vanilla` (714), while the styled perf runtime's residual wrappers hold it to 434. `StyleX` reaches 523; the runtime libraries carry their per-request serialize, `emotion` 135 req/s.

attribution.why: The css-prop fold renders in 1.30 ms with a 0.049 ms library slice, just over `vanilla` (1.23 ms) which hand-writes the classes. The styled perf runtime pays 0.437 ms of library time for the `Yak` wrappers the fold could not remove across the `styled(Component)` boundary and reaches 2.11 ms. `emotion` spends 4.41 ms of 7.44 ms hashing, `styled-components` 1.88 ms in `generateAndInjectStyles`.

hydrate.why: The css-prop fold's flatter tree, one class and no wrapper, hydrates with `vanilla` at 46.4-46.6 ms; the styled perf runtime's residual wrappers cost it 53.7 ms. The runtime hashers inject and reflow, `emotion` 98.0 ms, `goober` 194 ms, `styled-components` 195 ms.

inp.why: Selecting a tab re-renders a small subtree; the static-class lanes do it in ~6.80-7.50 ms, a near tie, with the css-prop fold's lighter tree at the front (6.80 ms). The hashers re-touch their sheet, `styled-components` 12.5 ms, `goober` 14.2 ms, `emotion` 26.9 ms.

mount.why: Cold mount parses one static sheet, so `vanilla`, the css-prop fold and `StyleX` land at 91.8-95.2 ms with the styled perf runtime's wrappers at 100 ms. The runtime libraries add first-inject, `goober` 193 ms, `styled-components` 198 ms, `emotion` 224 ms.

renderTiming.why: One recalc everywhere; the composition method changes the JS render, not the browser's style pass. The runtime libraries' larger styleMs comes from parsing the injected sheet, not extra recalcs.

payload.why: The css-prop fold ships one class per element and almost no runtime, 2.39 kB gzipped, under `vanilla` (2.72 kB) and the smallest in the case; the styled perf runtime carries the wrapper runtime the fold left behind at 3.46 kB. Atomic and hash libraries are 4.4-6.3× larger, `styled-components` 15.9 kB, `emotion` 15.2 kB, `cnfast` 21.9 kB.

nsweep.why: At 4000 tab groups the residual styled wrapper compounds: the styled perf runtime reaches 67.1 ms, double the css-prop fold and `vanilla` (~30.7-32.9 ms), because a `Yak` still renders per group where the css-prop lane emits a flat class. This is the clearest read on what the styled fold leaves on the table for composed trees.

crossCase: `tabs` is the single-file twin of `multifile-composition` below. Here `FullWidthTabs` is declared and used in one module, so its `styled(Tabs)` use site can fold; in the split version the primitives are imported and the styled perf runtime's SSR figure drifts from 1.45 to 1.48 ms/1k, while the css-prop fold, which has no `styled(...)` wrapper to lose across the boundary, holds (0.842 to 0.915) and ships an identical 2.39 kB.
